title: Universal finite etale component scheme of a finite-type scheme over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. For every separated scheme $X$ of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], there exists a finite etale $k$-scheme $\Pi_k(X)$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism] and a $k$-morphism $q_X:X\to\Pi_k(X)$ with the following properties. For every finite etale $k$-scheme $E$, composition with $q_X$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_k(\Pi_k(X),E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,E)$. The assignment is functorial in $X$, with $q_Y\circ f=\Pi_k(f)\circ q_X$ for every $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$. For every second separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$, its canonical comparisons $\Pi_k(\operatorname{Spec}k)\cong\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\Pi_k(X\times_kY)\cong\Pi_k(X)\times_k\Pi_k(Y)$ are isomorphisms compatible with the $q$ maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. For every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the canonical comparison $\Pi_L(X_L)\cong\Pi_k(X)_L$ is an isomorphism identifying $q_{X_L}$ with $(q_X)_L$. For every point $t\in\Pi_k(X)$, the fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is nonempty and geometrically connected: after every field extension of its residue field [def-weil-residue-field], it is nonempty and has connected underlying space [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The fibres of the underlying map $|q_X|$ are exactly the connected components of $|X|$.

source.place: Propositions 1.29, 1.30(a,b), 1.31(a,b) and Remark 1.33, printed pp.15-16: construction of pi_0(X), universal property, product and field-extension comparisons, and geometrically connected fibres.

proof.text: Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The directed-union lemma gives the actual subalgebra $B=B_k(A)$. Fix an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$. Both $X$ and $X_\Omega$ are Noetherian by finite type over a field; let $N$ be the finite number of irreducible components of $X_\Omega$. For any $D\in\mathcal E_k(A)$, the etale algebra classification and the separable tensor splitting identify $D\otimes_k\Omega$ with $\Omega^d$, where $d=\dim_kD$. Since $X$ is quasi-compact (finite type over $k$) and quasi-separated (separated implies quasi-separated), flat base change identifies $A\otimes_k\Omega$ with $\Gamma(X_\Omega,\mathcal O)$; tensoring the injection $D\subseteq A$ remains injective (extend a $k$-basis of $D$ to one of $A$). Thus the $d$ coordinate idempotents give $d$ disjoint nonempty clopens of $X_\Omega$ partitioning it. Every irreducible component lies in one part, so $d\le N$. The nonempty set of such dimensions has a largest member; choose $D_0$ attaining it. For every $D$, directedness gives $D'\supseteq D,D_0$ in the family. Maximal dimension forces $D'=D_0$, so $D\subseteq D_0$ and $B=D_0$ is finite etale. This also handles empty $X$: then $A=B=0$, $N=0$ and $d=0$.

source.place: Proposition 1.29, printed p.15; the preceding idempotent discussion, with the finite-type and flat-base-change inputs made explicit

proof.text: Define $\Pi_k(X)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and let $q_X$ correspond to the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow A$ under the morphism-into-affine bijection. This is real algebraic data, and step 1 makes $\Pi_k(X)$ finite etale. Let $E$ be finite etale over $k$. A finite morphism is affine, so $E=\operatorname{Spec}C$ for its finite-dimensional algebra $C$. A map $X\to E$ corresponds exactly to a $k$-algebra map $C\to A$ (the $k$-linearity is the equation on structure maps). By the directed-union lemma its image lies in $B$, and it factors uniquely as $C\to B\hookrightarrow A$. Applying the same affine bijection gives exactly the claimed bijection under composition with $q_X$.

source.place: Proposition 1.29 and the paragraph defining pi_0(X), printed p.15

proof.text: For $f:X\to Y$, define $\Pi_k(f)$ to be the unique map whose composite with $q_X$ is $q_Yf$, using step 2 with $E=\Pi_k(Y)$. Uniqueness proves the identity and composition laws and the displayed naturality equation. For $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $A=k$ and its finite etale subalgebra $k$ already equals $A$; hence $B=k$ and $q_X$ is the identity. This gives the canonical terminal comparison and its compatibility.

source.place: Universal property following Proposition 1.29; the terminal-object clause of the item

proof.text: For any field extension $L/k$, $X_L$ is again separated of finite type over $L$ by separated finite-type base change, so $\Pi_L(X_L)$ is defined. $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (it is finite type, and separated implies quasi-separated), so flat base change gives the canonical ring isomorphism $A\otimes_kL\cong\Gamma(X_L,\mathcal O)$. Apply the maximal ind-etale scalar-extension lemma to this algebra: $B_L(\Gamma(X_L,\mathcal O))=B_k(A)\otimes_kL$. Taking spectra, and identifying $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kL)$ with the fibre product $\Pi_k(X)\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ by the affine fibre-product lemma, gives $\Pi_L(X_L)\cong\Pi_k(X)_L$. The ring map defining $q_{X_L}$ is the scalar extension of the inclusion defining $q_X$, so this comparison identifies the actual maps, not just their isomorphism classes. By the uniqueness in step 2 it is the canonical comparison.

source.place: Proposition 1.30(a), printed p.15, and the sentence after its proof on p.16; algebraic form supplied by Stacks 0CKU

proof.text: Write $B=\prod_{i\in I}k_i$ by the etale algebra classification. Its points are the finitely many clopen spectra of the $k_i$. The point $t_i$ is the open set $D(e_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$, and the morphism-into-affine lemma gives $q_X^{-1}(D(e_i))=X_{e_i}=U_{e_i}$. Since $\{t_i\}\cong\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ is an open subscheme, the open fibre-product lemma identifies the scheme fibre $X_i=X\times_{\Pi_k(X)}\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ with the open subscheme $U_{e_i}$ of $X$. A coordinate idempotent $e_i\ne0$ stays nonzero in $A$, so its corresponding clopen $|X_i|$ is nonempty. If $|X_i|$ were disconnected, a nontrivial clopen partition of it would also be a clopen partition inside $X$, and hence would give an idempotent $e\in A$ with $e_ie=e$ and $e\ne0,e_i$. Every idempotent of $A$ lies in $B$ by the directed-union lemma. But the only idempotents in the field factor $e_iB=k_i$ are $0$ and $e_i$, a contradiction. Therefore these fibres are connected. A connected subset of $X$ cannot meet two disjoint clopen $X_i$, so the nonempty fibres are exactly its connected components.

source.place: Proposition 1.31(a), printed p.16; explicit idempotent proof of the sentence pi(X_x)=kappa(x)

proof.text: For a point $t$ with residue field $F=k_i$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/F$. Step 4 identifies $(q_X)_\Omega$ with $q_{X_\Omega}$. The embedding $F\hookrightarrow\Omega$ gives a rational point $s$ of $\Pi_k(X)_\Omega$, and associativity of fibre products identifies $(X_t)_\Omega$ with the fibre of $q_{X_\Omega}$ over $s$. Step 5 applied over $\Omega$ makes that fibre nonempty and connected. The algebraic-closure criterion for geometric connectedness, applied to the $F$-scheme $X_t$, now shows that it stays nonempty and connected after every field extension of $F$. No perfection assumption on $k$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 1.31(b), printed p.16, with the geometric connectedness criterion made explicit

proof.text: Set $T=\Pi_k(X)\times_k\Pi_k(Y)$. This is finite etale: its projection to $\Pi_k(X)$ is the base change of the etale structure map of $\Pi_k(Y)$, and composing with the etale structure map of $\Pi_k(X)$ is etale. By the affine fibre-product lemma $T=\operatorname{Spec}(B_X\otimes_kB_Y)$ for the coordinate algebras $B_X,B_Y$; the tensor products of finite bases of the two coordinate algebras span the tensor product, so $T$ is finite over $k$ by the definition of finite. By step 2 the map $(q_X,q_Y):X\times_kY\to T$ factors uniquely through a comparison $c:\Pi_k(X\times_kY)\to T$. The source product is again separated finite type: finite type is stable under base change and composition, and separatedness follows because under $(X\times_kY)\times_k(X\times_kY)\cong(X\times_kX)\times_k(Y\times_kY)$ its diagonal is $\Delta_X\times_k\Delta_Y$, a closed immersion by the closed-immersion products lemma. Thus the previous steps apply to it.

source.place: Proposition 1.30(b), printed pp.15-16; construction of the canonical product comparison

proof.text: Pass to a separable closure $k^s/k$. By the etale fibre description, a finite etale $k^s$-scheme is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ (a finite separable extension of a separably closed field has degree one). By steps 4-5, $X_{k^s}$ and $Y_{k^s}$ are partitioned into their nonempty connected fibres $U_i$ and $V_j$ over the points of the two component schemes. Each $U_i$ is geometrically connected by the separably-closed-field lemma, and the product-components lemma applied to $U_i\times V_j\to V_j$ says that $U_i\times V_j$ has one connected component, hence is nonempty and connected. These products are the disjoint clopen pieces of $(X\times Y)_{k^s}$, so they are exactly its components. Step 5 for the product identifies the geometric-point map induced by $c$ with the bijection from these components to the pairs $(i,j)$. This map is Galois equivariant because $c$ is defined over $k$. The inverse bijection is equivariant too. Full faithfulness of the geometric-point functor on etale $k$-schemes lifts this inverse to a morphism $T\to\Pi_k(X\times Y)$; faithfulness makes its two composites the identities. Hence $c$ is an isomorphism. Its compatibility with the $q$ maps is its defining equation. If either scheme is empty, both index sets of pairs and both component schemes of the product are empty, and the same argument applies.

source.place: Proposition 1.30(b), printed p.16; Remark 1.33(a); full-faithfulness descent of the component bijection
